e-4932.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Vector
e-4932.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(-3,2,1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $\mathbf{n}= \langle 0, 2, 0 \rangle.$
e-4932.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -3,2,1 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{n}=\langle 0,2,0 \rangle$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $\mathbf{n}$ can be given as

$$
(\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{p}) \cdot \mathbf{n} = 0,
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $\mathbf p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,2,0⟩ & =⟨-3,2,1⟩\cdot ⟨0,2,0⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,2,0⟩ & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4933.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector That Is Parallel To a Plane
e-4933.problem: A nonzero vector $\langle 0,\, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{b}, \: \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{c} \rangle$ is parallel to the plane $\mathbf{r} \cdot \langle 2, -1, 4 \rangle  = 3.$ What is the value of $\dfrac{b}{c}?$
e-4933.worked_solution:
We need a vector $\mathbf{v} = \langle t_1,t_2,t_3 \rangle$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $\mathbf{r} \cdot \langle 2, -1, 4 \rangle  = 3$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $\mathbf{n}=\langle 2, -1, 4 \rangle.$ So, $\mathbf{v} \perp \mathbf{n}$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨2,-1,4⟩ & =0 \\ 2{t}_{1}-{t}_{2}+4{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =2{t}_{1}+4{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
\mathbf{v}=\langle t_1, 2t_1 + 4t_3, t_3 \rangle,
$$

where $t_1,t_3 \in (-\infty,\infty).$ 

We are told that the first component of $\mathbf{v}$ equals $0.$ So, we must set $t_1=0.$ 

Since $\mathbf{v}$ is nonzero, we can pick any $t_3 \neq 0.$ For example, setting $t_3=1$, we get

$$
\mathbf{v} = \langle 0,\, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{4}, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1} \rangle.
$$

Therefore, $\dfrac{b}{c} = 4.$

e-4935.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
e-4935.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(\sqrt{2},0,-5)$ and is perpendicular to the line

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3 \\ y=-1+\sqrt{3}t \\ z=5-t.\end{aligned}
$$
e-4935.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $\mathbf{q}=\langle \sqrt{2},0,-5 \rangle.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083941/assets/3c1e2e4034bcbc860f548935ca7305bc8f141c56ba14f821fd1aa6cb2b53f8d9.png)

The direction vector of the line is $\mathbf{v}=\langle  0 , \sqrt{3} , -1\rangle,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
\mathbf{n}=\mathbf{v}=\langle  0 , \sqrt{3} , -1 \rangle.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ & =⟨\sqrt{2},0,-5⟩\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point P(2,−5,3) and is perpendicular to the vector n=⟨−1,2,−3⟩.

a
r⋅⟨2,−5,3⟩=21
b
r⋅⟨−1,2,−3⟩=⟨−2,5,−3⟩
c

decision.explanation: The given vector is normal to the plane, so r·n=P·n. Compute P·n=2(-1)+(-5)(2)+3(-3)=-21. Thus option e gives the required plane.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(2,-5,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨-1,2,-3⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,-5,3⟩,$ and $n=⟨-1,2,-3⟩$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ & =⟨2,-5,3⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ & =-21.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point P(2,−5,3) and is perpendicular to the vector n=⟨−1,2,−3⟩.

a
r⋅⟨2,−5,3⟩=21
b
r⋅⟨−1,2,−3⟩=⟨−2,5,−3⟩
c
r⋅⟨−1,2,−3⟩=−3
d
r⋅⟨2,−5,3⟩=⟨−1,2,−3⟩
e
r⋅⟨−1,2,−3⟩=−21
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=⟨2,−5,3⟩, and n=⟨−1,2,−3⟩ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point P(x0,y0,z0) and is perpendicular to the vector n can be given as (r−p)⋅n=0, where r is the position vector of any point on the plane, and p is the position vector of P.

So, we have (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n−p⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−1,2,−3⟩=⟨2,−5,3⟩⋅⟨−1,2,−3⟩r⋅⟨−1,2,−3⟩=−21.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms r·n=p·n. Since 2(-1)+(-5)(2)+3(-3)=-21, option e is correct. Option c, the deliberately incorrect submission, does not contain P.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Vector
content.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(2,-5,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨-1,2,-3⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,-5,3⟩,$ and $n=⟨-1,2,-3⟩$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ & =⟨2,-5,3⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,2,-3⟩ & =-21.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point P(1,−4,5) and is perpendicular to the vector n=[362].

a
 r⋅[1−45]=[362]
b
 r⋅[362]=[1−45]
c
 r⋅[362]=−20
d
 r⋅[1−45]=9
e
 r⋅[362]=−11
Submit

decision.explanation: The plane satisfies r·n=P·n, with normal n=(3,6,2). Since P·n=1(3)+(-4)(6)+5(2)=-11, option e is correct.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-4,5)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $n=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ is normal to the plane. 

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point P(1,−4,5) and is perpendicular to the vector n=[362].

a
 r⋅[1−45]=[362]
b
 r⋅[362]=[1−45]
c
 r⋅[362]=−20
d
 r⋅[1−45]=9
e
 r⋅[362]=−11
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the position vector of P is p=[1−45] and n=[362] is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point P(x0,y0,z0) and is perpendicular to the vector n can be given as (r−p)⋅n=0, where r is the position vector of any point on the plane, and p is the position vector of P.

So, we have (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n−p⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅[362]=[1−45]⋅[362]r⋅[362]=−11.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that r·n=p·n=1(3)+(-4)(6)+5(2)=-11. Thus option e has the required normal and passes through P.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Vector
content.problem: Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-4,5)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $n=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ is normal to the plane. 

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point P(5,−1,2) and is perpendicular to the vector n=5i−3j+2k.

a
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=6
b
 r⋅(5i−j−2k)=12
c
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=1
d
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=12
e
 r⋅(5i+2j−3k)=6
Submit

decision.explanation: The given vector is normal to the plane, so r·n=P·n=(√5)(√5)+(-1)(-3)+2(2)=5+3+4=12. Thus option d is correct.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(\sqrt{5},-1,2)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=\sqrt{5}i-j+2k,$ and $n=\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) & =(\sqrt{5}i-j+2k)\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) \\ r\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point P(5,−1,2) and is perpendicular to the vector n=5i−3j+2k.

a
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=6
b
 r⋅(5i−j−2k)=12
c
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=1
d
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=12
e
 r⋅(5i+2j−3k)=6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=5i−j+2k, and n=5i−3j+2k is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point P(x0,y0,z0) and is perpendicular to the vector n can be given as (r−p)⋅n=0, where r is the position vector of any point on the plane, and p is the position vector of P.

So, we have (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n−p⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅(5i−3j+2k)=(5i−j+2k)⋅(5i−3j+2k)r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=12.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Vector
content.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(\sqrt{5},-1,2)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=\sqrt{5}i-j+2k,$ and $n=\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) & =(\sqrt{5}i-j+2k)\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) \\ r\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point Q(1,2,−1) and is perpendicular to the vector n=[2−43].

a
r⋅[12−1]=−9
b
r⋅[12−1]=[24−3]
c
r⋅[2−43]=−9
d
r⋅[2−43]=[12−1]
e
r⋅[12−1]=−5
Submit

decision.explanation: The given vector is normal to the plane, so r·n=Q·n=1(2)+2(-4)+(-1)(3)=-9. Therefore option c gives the required plane.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $Q(1,2,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $n=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $Q({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-q)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$

So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point Q(1,2,−1) and is perpendicular to the vector n=[2−43].

a
r⋅[12−1]=−9
b
r⋅[12−1]=[24−3]
c
r⋅[2−43]=−9
d
r⋅[2−43]=[12−1]
e
r⋅[12−1]=−5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, note that the position vector of Q is q=[12−1] and n=[2−43] is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point Q(x0,y0,z0) and is perpendicular to the vector n can be given as (r−q)⋅n=0, where r is the position vector of any point on the plane, and q is the position vector of Q.

So, we have (r−q)⋅n=0r⋅n−q⋅n=0r⋅n=q⋅nr⋅[2−43]=[12−1]⋅[2−43]r⋅[2−43]=−9.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Vector
content.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $Q(1,2,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $n=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $Q({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-q)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$

So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,b,\,0⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩=-14.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
after.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩=-14$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨6,-2,0⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨6,-2,0⟩ & =0 \\ 6{t}_{1}-2{t}_{2} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =3{t}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},3{t}_{1},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the third component of $v$ eqauls $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{3}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{1}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{1}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{3}.$

after.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,0,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-1,2,2⟩=\sqrt{11}.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-1,2,2⟩=\sqrt{11}$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-1,2,2⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,2,2⟩ & =0 \\ -{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}+2{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{1} & =2{t}_{2}+2{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨2{t}_{2}+2{t}_{3},\,{t}_{2},\,{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{2},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the second component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{2}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨2,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{c}=2.$

Question 8
?

A nonzero vector ⟨a,b,0⟩ is parallel to the plane r⋅⟨−5,−1,4⟩=6. What is the value of ab?

a
−54
b
−15
c
5
d
15
e
14
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We need a vector v=⟨t1,t2,t3⟩ that is parallel to the given plane.

From the equation r⋅⟨−5,−1,4⟩=6 of the plane, we get the normal vector n=⟨−5,−1,4⟩. So, v⊥n and we have the following:

v⋅n=0⟨t1,t2,t3⟩⋅⟨−5,−1,4⟩=0−5t1−t2+4t3=0t2=−5t1+4t3

Hence, we obtain v=⟨t1,−5t1+4t3,t3⟩, where t1,t3∈(−∞,∞).

We are told that the third component of v equals 0. So, we must set t3=0.

Since v is nonzero, we can pick any t1≠0. For example, setting t1=1, we get

v=⟨1,−5,0⟩.

Therefore, ab=−15.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms -5a-b=0, so b=-5a. Since the vector is nonzero, b≠0 and a/b=-1/5. This matches option b.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector That Is Parallel To a Plane
content.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,b,\,0⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-5,-1,4⟩=6.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
content.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-5,-1,4⟩=6$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-5,-1,4⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-5,-1,4⟩ & =0 \\ -5{t}_{1}-{t}_{2}+4{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =-5{t}_{1}+4{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},-5{t}_{1}+4{t}_{3},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the third component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{3}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{1}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{1}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨1,\,-5,\,0⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{b}=-\frac{1}{5}.$

after.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,0,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨4,0,2⟩=16.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨4,0,2⟩ & =0 \\ 4{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3} & =0 \\ 2{t}_{3} & =-4{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{3} & =-2{t}_{1}\end{aligned}

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,{t}_{2},\,-2{t}_{1}⟩,

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{1}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{1}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩.

a

b
−12

12
d
4
e

Correct

We need a vector v=⟨t1,t2,t3⟩ that is parallel to the given plane.

From the equation r⋅⟨4,0,2⟩=16 of the plane, we get the normal vector n=⟨4,0,2⟩. So, v⊥n and we have the following:

v⋅n=0⟨t1,t2,t3⟩⋅⟨4,0,2⟩=04t1+2t3=02t3=−4t1t3=−2t1

Hence, we obtain v=⟨t1,t2,−2t1⟩, where t1,t2∈(−∞,∞).

We are told that the second component of v equals 0. So, we must set t2=0.

Since v is nonzero, we can pick any t1≠0. For example, setting t1=1, we get

v=⟨1,0,−2⟩.

Therefore, ac=−12.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩=7.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩=7$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-3,1,-2⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩ & =0 \\ -3{t}_{1}+{t}_{2}-2{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3},\,{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=2.$

Question 10

A nonzero vector ⟨0,b,c⟩ is parallel to the plane r⋅⟨−3,1,−2⟩=7. What is the value of bc?

a
3
b
−3
c
2
d
12
e
−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need a vector v=⟨t1,t2,t3⟩ that is parallel to the given plane.

From the equation r⋅⟨−3,1,−2⟩=7 of the plane, we get the normal vector n=⟨−3,1,−2⟩. So, v⊥n and we have the following:

v⋅n=0⟨t1,t2,t3⟩⋅⟨−3,1,−2⟩=0−3t1+t2−2t3=0t2=3t1+2t3

Hence, we obtain v=⟨t1,3t1+2t3,t3⟩, where t1,t3∈(−∞,∞).

We are told that the first component of v equals 0. So, we must set t1=0.

Since v is nonzero, we can pick any t3≠0. For example, setting t3=1, we get

v=⟨0,2,1⟩.

Therefore, bc=2.

c

decision.explanation: The line's direction vector ⟨1,-1,2⟩ is normal to the plane. Therefore r·⟨1,-1,2⟩=⟨2,1,-3⟩·⟨1,-1,2⟩=2-1-6=-5, giving option e.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(2,1,-3)$ and is  perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=3+2t.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨2,1,-3⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=3+2t\end{aligned}\,⇒\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨1,2,3⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨1,-1,2⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

   

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨1,-1,2⟩.$ So, a normal  vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨1,-1,2⟩.
$$

 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =⟨2,1,-3⟩\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=3+2t.\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨2,1,-3⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$

   

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨1,-1,2⟩.$ So, a normal  vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨1,-1,2⟩.
$$

 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =⟨2,1,-3⟩\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(2,1,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(2,1,0)$ and $B(3,2,1).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨2,1,-1⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(2,1,0)$ and $B(3,2,1)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨3,2,1⟩-⟨2,1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨1,1,1⟩.$ 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,1⟩ & =⟨2,1,-1⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,1⟩ & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point Q(2,1,−1) and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points A(2,1,0) and B(3,2,1).

a
r⋅⟨1,1,1⟩=⟨2,1,−1⟩
b
r⋅⟨1,1,1⟩=0
c
r⋅⟨2,1,−1⟩=⟨1,1,1⟩
d
r⋅⟨1,1,1⟩=2
e
r⋅⟨2,1,−1⟩=2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of Q is q=⟨2,1,−1⟩.

Since the line passes through the points A(2,1,0) and B(3,2,1) we can find a vector parallel to the line:

AB→=⟨3,2,1⟩−⟨2,1,0⟩=⟨1,1,1⟩.

So, a normal vector to the plane is n=⟨1,1,1⟩.

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by (r−q)⋅n=0r⋅n−q⋅n=0r⋅n=q⋅nr⋅⟨1,1,1⟩=⟨2,1,−1⟩⋅⟨1,1,1⟩r⋅⟨1,1,1⟩=2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that B−A=⟨1,1,1⟩ is normal to the plane. Its dot product with Q is 2+1−1=2, so option d is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
content.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(2,1,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(2,1,0)$ and $B(3,2,1).$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨2,1,-1⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(2,1,0)$ and $B(3,2,1)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨3,2,1⟩-⟨2,1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨1,1,1⟩.$ 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,1⟩ & =⟨2,1,-1⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,1⟩ & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(-3,2,1)$ and is  perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+6t \\ y=3-5t \\ z=-2+4t.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨-3,2,1⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+6t \\ y=3-5t \\ z=-2+4t\end{aligned}\,⇒\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨-1,3,-2⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨6,-5,4⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

   

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨6,-5,4⟩.$ So, a normal  vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨6,-5,4⟩.
$$

 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ & =⟨-3,2,1⟩\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ & =-24.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
content.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(-3,2,1)$ and is  perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+6t \\ y=3-5t \\ z=-2+4t.\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨-3,2,1⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+6t \\ y=3-5t \\ z=-2+4t\end{aligned}\,⇒\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨-1,3,-2⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨6,-5,4⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

   

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨6,-5,4⟩.$ So, a normal  vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨6,-5,4⟩.
$$

 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ & =⟨-3,2,1⟩\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ & =-24.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 14
?

Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point Q(1,−4,2) and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points A(2,1,−3) and B(1,6,−4).

a
r⋅⟨−1,5,−1⟩=⟨1,−4,2⟩
b
r⋅⟨−1,5,−1⟩=0
c
r⋅⟨−1,5,−1⟩=−23
d
r⋅⟨1,−4,2⟩=−23
e
r⋅⟨1,−4,2⟩=⟨−1,5,−1⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The line's direction B−A=⟨-1,5,-1⟩ is normal to the plane. Its dot product with Q is 1(-1)+(-4)(5)+2(-1)=-23, so option c is correct.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(1,-4,2)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(2,1,-3)$ and $B(1,6,-4).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨1,-4,2⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(2,1,-3)$ and $B(1,6,-4)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,6,-4⟩-⟨2,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,5,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-1,5,-1⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ & =⟨1,-4,2⟩\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ & =-23.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(1,-4,2)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(2,1,-3)$ and $B(1,6,-4).$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨1,-4,2⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(2,1,-3)$ and $B(1,6,-4)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,6,-4⟩-⟨2,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,5,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-1,5,-1⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ & =⟨1,-4,2⟩\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-1,5,-1⟩ & =-23.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨1,-2,3⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(4,1,-3)$ and $B(7,-3,1)$, we can find a vector that is parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨7,-3,1⟩-⟨4,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-4,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨3,-4,4⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ & =⟨1,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ & =23.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of Q is q=⟨1,−2,3⟩.

Since the line passes through the points A(4,1,−3) and B(7,−3,1), we can find a vector that is parallel to the line:

AB→=⟨7,−3,1⟩−⟨4,1,−3⟩=⟨3,−4,4⟩

So, a normal vector to the plane is n=⟨3,−4,4⟩.

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

(r−q)⋅n=0r⋅n−q⋅n=0r⋅n=q⋅nr⋅⟨3,−4,4⟩=⟨1,−2,3⟩⋅⟨3,−4,4⟩r⋅⟨3,−4,4⟩=23.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
content.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(1,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(4,1,-3)$ and $B(7,-3,1).$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨1,-2,3⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(4,1,-3)$ and $B(7,-3,1)$, we can find a vector that is parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨7,-3,1⟩-⟨4,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-4,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨3,-4,4⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ & =⟨1,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ & =23.\end{aligned}
$$
